# PORT M1 §11 — GENERATION TRUTH AUDIT (D-069)

Generated by `engine/port_m1/report_genaudit.py`. Spec `design/PORT_M1_SPEC.md` §11 sha16 `12f0a849107b2d3f` (D-069). Engine `engine/port_m1/gen_audit.py`, plots `engine/port_m1/plot_genaudit.py`, red-first `engine/port_m1/test_genaudit.py`. Roster = the frozen v3 oracle (`ORACLE_FREEZE.tsv` shas verified at run start). Every number carries its source `file:line`.

## Outcome

The roster reaches **89.5%/89.5%/89.5% of the perfect-knowledge ceiling** (dollar-weighted, all eras): SI CEIL $4,060 vs roster $3,608 median/session, HG CEIL $2,892 vs roster $2,572 median/session, NKD CEIL $3,235 vs roster $2,872 median/session. What is left on the table is small and it is NOT missing legs — it is timing and the phase-close exit, in that order. The four buckets and the per-leg timing distributions are below; the decomposition is the STANDING regression metric from here on (baseline frozen in `forfeit_sessions.tsv`).

- **SI: COVERED — the roster already fires through the middle of the leg.** Deciles 2-7 (60% of the leg's clock) carry 49.8% of the same-side candidates; at the halfway mark the median leg still has $625 ahead of it, and the thinnest middle decile still has a candidate on 68% of legs.
- **HG: COVERED — the roster already fires through the middle of the leg.** Deciles 2-7 (60% of the leg's clock) carry 50.5% of the same-side candidates; at the halfway mark the median leg still has $469 ahead of it, and the thinnest middle decile still has a candidate on 69% of legs.
- **NKD: COVERED — the roster already fires through the middle of the leg.** Deciles 2-7 (60% of the leg's clock) carry 50.7% of the same-side candidates; at the halfway mark the median leg still has $538 ahead of it, and the thinnest middle decile still has a candidate on 69% of legs.

Rule applied (pre-registered, and style-agnostic per D-070 — no family class is preferred, only measured dollars): a CONTINUATION/PULLBACK family hypothesis is raised (routed to `family_discovery`, D-055; it would enter as a new CLASS under D-071) only when the middle six deciles hold < 30% of candidates AND the median leg still has >= $1,000 ahead at the halfway mark — value present AND uncovered. Neither asset meets the trigger: the roster's candidate density is nearly FLAT across the leg (the mild edge peaks at d0 are the confirmation itself and the next leg's setup), so the reversal-shape coverage gap D-069 hypothesised is NOT present. The mid-leg dollars are covered by candidates that already exist; whether entering there PAYS is a selection question, not a generation gap.

| ceil_entry_superset | `superset_spine_only` | 4 | C1_block_min_at_block_end,C3_monotone_fall,C4_block_max_at_block_end,C5_step_shocks | `artifacts/cache/port/m1/gen_audit/redfirst.tsv:8` |

### Why the CEIL entry superset is exact

The ceiling admits entries at ANY SANE second, which is ~80,000 x 2 items per session. The reduction is a proof, not a sample:

1. The phase-close certificate's exit second `pc(t)` depends only on t's phase block, so every entry in one block shares one exit.
2. With the exit fixed, value_long(t) = (mid(exit) - mid(t)) x mult - cost is maximised at the block's argmin mid (argmax for short).
3. That argmin cannot hit the wall: every SANE second after it and before the boundary has a mid at or above it, and the boundary second IS the exit — if the exit mid were below the argmin, no long in that block has positive value at all and nothing is seated. So the unconstrained maximiser is feasible, hence optimal.
4. The DP's only coupling is `start > previous exit`, which can exclude at most the block's first second; the block-argmin restricted to `t > first` covers that case.

The implemented superset is the fine-grain (1-tick) ZigZag spine UNION those landmarks. **The spine alone is NOT complete** — a block extremum that never retraces by a tick before the block ends is never confirmed as a pivot — and that is exactly the `superset_spine_only` mutant above, caught by brute force on 4 of 6 synthetic paths. It is NOT caught on the three brute-forced real sessions (SI 2021-11-28, 2021-07-25, 2022-08-21), which is the reason the landmarks are in the production superset rather than trusted to a spot check: real sessions are dense enough that the spine usually happens to contain the extremum, so a spine-only implementation would have passed a real-data test and silently deflated the ceiling on the sessions where it matters.

## Defects and interpretive notes

- **GA-1 (found, fixed, receipted).** The m0 path skeleton stores its adverse running-max records as `float32` (`engine/port_m0/c_c_roster.py:253`), so the roster's wall test is a float32 comparison: an adverse excursion of 899.9999999999986 rounds UP to exactly 900.0 there and kills a certificate a float64 test keeps. The ceiling therefore uses the SAME float32 arithmetic (`engine/port_m1/gen_audit.py` `SessionValues`), or CEIL < ROSTER becomes possible on those boundary candidates. `test_genaudit.py` `t_ceil_dominates_roster` asserts value-function == m0-certificate candidate by candidate.
- **GA-2 (spec reading, declared).** §11.B lists EXIT_FORFEIT as a bucket of `CEIL - ROSTER`, but both DPs exit at the phase close, so 'value beyond phase-close' can only enter that difference when the roster's best entry is cut by a boundary the leg runs past. EXIT_FORFEIT is implemented that way (the leg's ceiling-minus-roster gap, conditional on `best_cand_phase_close_sec < leg_end_sec`). The literal 'dollars beyond the phase close' figure is reported BESIDE it, unallocated, as `beyond_phase_close_usd` in `leg_capture_profile.tsv` — it is large and it is the exit program's prize, not generation's forfeit.
- **GA-3 (declared).** §11.C says '20 sessions/asset stratified by (era x offer quartile)' without defining the era axis for this purpose; calendar years 2021-2025 x 4 quartiles gives exactly the 20 the spec asks for and is what is implemented (`gen_audit.py` `strata`).
- **GA-4 (declared).** The forfeit decomposition is a per-session accounting identity, not an inference; no p-values are claimed, so CC-M1-12.4's cluster-robust caveat binds nothing here. Where the report compares eras it compares medians of a full population, not estimates from a sample.
- **GA-5 (declared).** OCCUPANCY is the residual by construction (§11.B), so it also absorbs any attribution slack: a leg's ceiling value can exceed what a one-position scheduler could ever have seated, and legs overlap. Raw (uncapped) bucket dollars are carried beside the allocated ones (`*_raw_usd`) so the cap is auditable.
